A union of a dozen string literals is a list you look things up in, and that only works when it is in order. This rule keeps the members of every union type sorted alphabetically, ignoring case, by how they are written in the source. `--fix` reorders them.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-union-types" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default. The ones that are commented out are unset by default.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-union-types" = ["error", {
  type = "alphabetical",
  order = "asc", # "asc" or "desc"
  ignoreCase = true,
  specialCharacters = "keep", # "remove", "trim" or "keep"
  alphabet = "", # string
  locales = "en-US",
  fallbackSort = {
    type = "unsorted",
    # order = <"asc" or "desc">,
  },
  groups = [],
  customGroups = [], # list of objects
  newlinesBetween = "ignore", # "ignore" or number
  newlinesInside = "newlinesBetween", # "ignore", number or "newlinesBetween"
  partitionByNewLine = false,
  partitionByComment = false,
  useConfigurationIf = {
    # allNamesMatchPattern = <list of objects or strings, object or string>,
    # matchesAstSelector = <string>,
  },
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
type Status = "pending" | "active" | "done";
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
type Status = "active" | "done" | "pending";
```

## Options

The rule takes one or more configuration objects. With more than one, the first whose `useConfigurationIf` matches the union applies to it.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"alphabetical"` | How to compare members. `"natural"` treats digits as numbers, so `"2px"` comes before `"10px"`. `"line-length"` sorts by the length of the member. `"custom"` sorts by `alphabet`. `"unsorted"` leaves the order alone and only applies `groups`. `"subgroup-order"` sorts by the position of the group inside a nested list in `groups`. |
| `order` | `"asc"` | `"desc"` reverses the order. |
| `ignoreCase` | `true` | Compare members in lower case. |
| `specialCharacters` | `"keep"` | `"trim"` ignores characters other than letters at the start of a member, `"remove"` ignores them everywhere. |
| `alphabet` | `""` | The characters in the order they sort in, for `type: "custom"`. |
| `locales` | `"en-US"` | The locale that `"alphabetical"` and `"natural"` compare members in. |
| `fallbackSort` | `{ type: "unsorted" }` | How to order two members that the main comparison finds equal: `type`, and optionally `order`. |
| `groups` | `[]` | The order of the groups. A nested list makes several groups count as one. Members that match no group come last, or where `"unknown"` is. |
| `customGroups` | `[]` | Groups of your own: `{ groupName, elementNamePattern }`, `selector`, or `anyOf` with a list of those. A custom group can also carry its own `type`, `order`, `fallbackSort` and `newlinesInside`. |
| `newlinesBetween` | `"ignore"` | The number of empty lines between groups, `0` for none. A `{ newlinesBetween }` entry in `groups` sets it between two groups. |
| `newlinesInside` | `"newlinesBetween"` | The number of empty lines between two members of the same group, `"ignore"` to leave them alone. The default follows `newlinesBetween`. |
| `partitionByNewLine` | `false` | Sort each block of members that is separated by an empty line on its own. |
| `partitionByComment` | `false` | `true`: a comment between two members separates two blocks that are sorted on their own. A pattern or a list of patterns: only a comment that matches. `{ block, line }`: separately for `/* */` and `//` comments. |
| `useConfigurationIf` | `{}` | When this configuration applies: `allNamesMatchPattern`, a pattern every member must match, or `matchesAstSelector`, an ESLint selector the union must match. |

The groups a member can fall in, by what kind of type it is:

| Group | Members |
| --- | --- |
| `"named"` | A type name such as `User`, `User["id"]`, `User[]` or `infer T` |
| `"keyword"` | `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `bigint`, `symbol`, `object`, `any`, `unknown`, `never`, `this` |
| `"literal"` | `"active"`, `1`, `true` or a template literal type |
| `"nullish"` | `null`, `undefined`, `void` |
| `"function"` | A function or constructor type |
| `"object"` | An object type `{ .. }` or a mapped type |
| `"tuple"` | `[string, number]` |
| `"operator"` | `keyof T`, `typeof x`, `readonly T[]` |
| `"conditional"` | `T extends U ? X : Y` |
| `"intersection"` | `A & B` |
| `"union"` | A nested union in parentheses |
| `"import"` | `import("./module").Type` |

### `type`

{/* bad {"options": [{"type": "natural"}]} */}
```ts
type Size = "10px" | "2px";
```

{/* good {"options": [{"type": "natural"}]} */}
```ts
type Size = "2px" | "10px";
```

### `groups`

Put type names first and `null` and `undefined` last:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-union-types" = ["error", {
  groups = ["named", "keyword", "literal", "nullish"],
}]
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"groups": ["named", "keyword", "literal", "nullish"]}]} */}
```ts
type Value = null | string | User | "none";
```

{/* good {"options": [{"groups": ["named", "keyword", "literal", "nullish"]}]} */}
```ts
type Value = User | string | "none" | null;
```

### `partitionByNewLine` and `partitionByComment`

An empty line or a comment keeps what is above it apart from what is below:

{/* good {"options": [{"partitionByNewLine": true}]} */}
```ts
type Event =
  | "click"
  | "keydown"

  | "blur"
  | "focus";
```

{/* good {"options": [{"partitionByComment": true}]} */}
```ts
type Event =
  | "click"
  | "keydown"
  // Focus events
  | "blur"
  | "focus";
```
